title: New Jersey AI Laws

reading.body:
New Jersey's only AI-related law targets algorithmic rent-setting, not AI development, and it does so through antitrust rather than AI regulation.

The FAIR Act, passed July 20, 2026, makes it unlawful for rental property owners to use coordinators that perform coordinating functions. It also reaches the coordinators themselves, parallel pricing coordination among two or more persons, and any person performing a coordinating function. Enforcement runs through the New Jersey Antitrust Act, and the Attorney General must establish a complaint location and may write rules.

This matters for AI because the mechanism is software that sets rents across many properties at once. The law names the algorithmic device as the instrument, which places it among the tools that aggregate data and produce coordinated pricing. It does not address data centers, power procurement, or the physical buildout that constrains AI scaling, and nothing in the enrolled text touches those subjects.

The data covers one law and no more. It does not say how many coordinators operate in New Jersey, what penalties apply, or whether the Attorney General has proposed rules. A single enacted law also cannot show a trend, so the absence of other New Jersey AI laws here reflects what this site tracks, not necessarily the full body of state law touching automated systems.

New Jersey has enacted 1 AI-related law. Each is read from its enrolled text: what it does, who it applies to, when it takes effect, and what it requires.

Enacted AI laws in New Jersey

1 law this site judged relevant to AI, newest first, each read from its enrolled text.

  • A3497: Establishes "Forbidding the Algorithmic Inflation of Rent (FAIR) Act." passed 2026-07-20

    The act makes it unlawful and a violation of the New Jersey Antitrust Act for rental property owners to use coordinators that perform coordinating functions, for coordinators to facilitate agreements among rental property owners that restrict competition, for two or more persons to engage in parallel pricing coordination, and for any person to perform a coordinating function. It defines key terms such as algorithmic device, coordinating function, and competitively sensitive information. It requires the Attorney General to establish a complaint location and authorizes rulemaking.

How this page is kept

This page is generated from the enacted laws this site tracks for New Jersey. When the legislature passes another AI-related bill, it appears here the night the bill's text is read. The full 50-state picture is at State AI Laws.
